caption:
Instagram already told you what it measures: watch time, likes per reach, and sends per reach. Named publicly by Adam Mosseri, Instagram's head, and restated through 2026.

Notice what is NOT on that list: follower count, hashtag count, posting at 7pm, comment pods.

And notice the two words doing all the work — per reach. A post with 40 likes from 300 people beats a post with 200 likes from 20,000. The second one looks better on a screenshot. The first one is the better post.

Save this and go do the exercise: open your last 10 posts, write down reach and sends for each, divide. That column is your real scoreboard, and almost nobody has ever looked at it.

If you are small, this is good news. Smaller accounts reach a bigger share of their own audience than large ones do. You do not need a big account. You need a high rate.
